name: CR-Int-15-partialfrac-4.c
questiontext:
By expressing the integrand as the sum of its partial fractions, find the following definite integral:
\[ \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}. \]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
In order to calculate \[\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}\] we need to express \[{{CT:2}}\] as the sum of its partial fractions <hint>alg_partial_fractions</hint>.

Omitting details we have \[{{CT:2}} = {{CT:4}},\]
hence,
\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int {{CT:4}} d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:5}} \int {{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}} + {{CT:7}} \int {{CT:8}} d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:9}} + {{CT:10}} +c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:11}} +c
 \end{array}\]

We need \[\int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}\] so, recall that if \[\int f(x) dx = F(x)\] then \[\int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b).\]

Thus, define \[F({{CT:3}}) = {{CT:12}}\]

Then,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
  \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:13}} - \left[{{CT:14}}\right] \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:15}}
 \end{array}\]
